category: biomedical literature index with an open-access full-text subset

free_tier.stated: REST access to 'over 33 million publications', including '10.2 million full text articles and 6.5 million open access articles', with JSON or XML responses and pageSize up to 1000.
free_tier.notes: pageSize=1000 returned 786,907 bytes of JSON in one response here; pageSize=100 returned 88,669 bytes.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: one JSON/XML response per request, paged. The largest single response measured was 786,907 bytes at pageSize=1000.

retention.stated: the index is continuously updated; the bulk FTP tree carries dated snapshots (weekly for metadata, per-release for the OA subset)

egress.terms: Free and unmetered from the EBI endpoint. No key, no account, no registration mentioned anywhere on the web-service page.

interface_detail: GET https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=...&format=json&pageSize=1000&cursorMark=...; eight bulk content types are listed at /downloads and served over FTP.
tooling: curl/python-requests for the API; lftp or curl for the FTP tree. No SDK needed.
chaining: Use Europe PMC as the index (PMIDs, PMCIDs, licence flags, full-text availability) and pmc-oa-opendata as the byte store; the API's pageSize=1000 gives about 787 KB of metadata per call without an account.

limits.value: no numeric rate limit is published; paging is by pageSize/cursorMark and the largest single page is pageSize=1000

limits_note: The bulk path is FTP and it did not answer from this network: https://europepmc.org/ftp/oa/ returned 403 and ftp://europepmc.org/oa/ timed out after 20 s. That is a reachability fact about for a user, not a statement that the mirror is gone.
binding_note: With the FTP mirror unreachable here, the API is the only path, and it is one page per call with no published ceiling: at 787 KB per pageSize=1000 call, a TiB would take about 1.4 million calls, so the call rate decides the day's bytes, not any byte quota.

identity_cost.detail: No key and no account: an anonymous GET returned 200 and 1,408 bytes. Nothing on the web-service page asks for registration.

reliability_note: No throttling signal was seen at the low rate used here; the FTP tree is the fragile part - one 403 on HTTPS and a timeout on port 21 make the bulk mirror look absent when it may only be filtered.
confidence_note: The API was exercised at two page sizes with byte counts, and the bulk-path failures were observed. The 33M/10.2M/6.5M counts are the vendor's own page, not independently measured.

evidence.proved: 'over 33 million publications', '10.2 million full text articles and 6.5 million open access articles', JSON/XML output
eight bulk content types (OA subset, author manuscripts, preprints, metadata, ID mappings, text-mined terms) served over FTP
200, 786,907 bytes in one anonymous response - pageSize=1000 is accepted and returns real records
403 over HTTPS - the FTP tree has no HTTPS mirror at that path

notes: Caveat is the bulk mirror, not the API. Metadata is effectively unlimited through pageSize=1000; full text at TiB scale depends on the FTP tree, which this network could not open.
